title: Academic Writing Task 1: comparing maps
status: Owner approved v1.0.0 on 2026-10-18; teacher release to all eligible schools (optional extension lesson)
rights: Original Brains Heist LLC instructional draft, AI-assisted. Places and maps are fictional, created for practice. Human editorial, model, mapping and originality review pending.
prerequisites: Lesson 11 (Task 1 overviews) and Lesson 19 (Task 1 tables and accuracy).
Teacher has checked actual Writing Screener and review states privately.
Optional extension: use when learners need practice with map tasks.

objectives.text: Write a map overview that states the general direction of change and what stayed the same.
Describe changes accurately with passive verbs of change and precise location phrases.
Organise changes by area so the reader can follow the map.

levels.foundation: Compass directions labelled first; overview frame and change bank allowed and recorded.
levels.core: Write an accurate overview and body paragraph in 15 minutes.
levels.extension: Use "to make way for" and a location phrase in every sentence.
levels.high_band: Produce a new 150+-word comparative map report in 20 minutes without a model. Organise by meaningful spatial contrasts, distinguish preserved from replaced features, and avoid unsupported speculation or inaccurate directional language.

blocks.title: Which overview works for maps?
blocks.mode: Teacher-led analysis; learners rank before the reveal
blocks.instructions: Three learners wrote an overview for the Westhill maps. Rank them and explain the problems in the weaker two.

examples.label: Overview A
examples.text: Overall, the farmland was replaced by a housing estate, the shops were replaced by a supermarket and the school was extended.
examples.comment: A list of details, not a summary: it gives three changes without saying what they mean together.

examples.label: Overview B
examples.text: Overall, Westhill has changed a lot and is now a better place to live.
examples.comment: Vague and opinion-based: the maps do not show whether the village is better.

examples.label: Overview C
examples.text: Overall, Westhill has become considerably more developed, with much of its farmland and forest giving way to housing and leisure facilities, although the main road and the river remain unchanged.
examples.comment: Best: it states the general direction of change and what stayed the same, without listing details.

blocks.title: Accurate or inaccurate?
blocks.mode: Guided practice; answer alone, then check
blocks.instructions: Look at the Westhill maps. Write Accurate or Inaccurate for each sentence. If it is inaccurate, correct it.

figure.title: Westhill village
figure.alt: Two maps of Westhill village. In 1995, farmland covered the north-west, a forest the north-east, a row of shops lay south of the main road in the west, a small school in the south-east, and a river ran along the southern edge. Today, the farmland has become a housing estate, part of the forest has been cleared for a sports centre, the shops have been replaced by a supermarket with a car park beside it, the school has been extended, and a new road crosses the river by a bridge.

items.prompt: The farmland in the north-west has been converted into a housing estate.
items.reason: 'Converted into' is a precise verb for a change of use.

items.prompt: The whole forest was cleared to make way for a sports centre.
items.evidence: Today: Forest still in the north-east, smaller
items.reason: Only part of the forest was cleared: 'part of the forest was cleared'.

items.prompt: The shops to the south of the main road have been replaced by a supermarket.
items.reason: 'Replaced by' is followed by the new building.

items.prompt: A car park has been built to the west of the supermarket.
items.evidence: Today: Car park is east of the supermarket
items.reason: Check direction words against the map: the car park is to the east.

items.prompt: The school in the south-east has been extended.
The river has been moved further south.
items.evidence: River in the same position on both maps
items.reason: The river is unchanged; a new road now crosses it by a bridge.

blocks.support: Foundation: the class first labels north, south, east and west on both maps and lists every building that changed.
blocks.extension: Rewrite each inaccurate sentence so that it is accurate and uses a passive verb.

blocks.title: Your overview and one body paragraph
blocks.mode: Independent classroom application after modelling; not a full Task 1 or Writing Screener
blocks.prompt: The maps show the village of Westhill in 1995 and today. Write an overview and a body paragraph describing the changes to the north of the main road.

figure.title: Westhill village
figure.alt: Two maps of Westhill village. In 1995, farmland covered the north-west, a forest the north-east, a row of shops lay south of the main road in the west, a small school in the south-east, and a river ran along the southern edge. Today, the farmland has become a housing estate, part of the forest has been cleared for a sports centre, the shops have been replaced by a supermarket with a car park beside it, the school has been extended, and a new road crosses the river by a bridge.

blocks.conditions: 15 minutes, independent. No model visible. Record any frame or phrase-bank use.
blocks.support: Overview frame: Overall, Westhill has become ..., with ..., although ... remain(s) unchanged. Change bank: was replaced by / was converted into / was cleared to make way for / was extended / was constructed.
blocks.extension: Use one "to make way for" and one location phrase in each sentence.
blocks.high_band: Produce a new 150+-word comparative map report in 20 minutes without a model. Organise by meaningful spatial contrasts, distinguish preserved from replaced features, and avoid unsupported speculation or inaccurate directional language.
blocks.model_label: Illustrative classroom model for discussion only. Not a certified band answer.
blocks.model:
Overall, Westhill has become considerably more developed since 1995, with much of its farmland and forest giving way to housing and leisure facilities, although the main road and the river remain unchanged.

The most striking changes have taken place to the north of the main road. The farmland that occupied the north-west of the village has been converted into a large housing estate. To the east of this, part of the forest has been cleared to make way for a new sports centre, so that only a smaller area of woodland now remains in the north-east corner.
checklist: Task Achievement: Is there an overview of the most important changes (and what stayed the same)? Are changes reported accurately?
Coherence and Cohesion: Are changes grouped logically, for example by area of the village, and linked clearly?
Lexical Resource: Is the vocabulary of change precise (was replaced by, was converted into, was cleared, was extended, was constructed)?
Grammatical Range and Accuracy: Are passive forms and the past simple / present perfect used accurately, with location phrases (to the north of, in the south-east)?

blocks.title: Complete Task 1 under time
blocks.mode: Timed homework under declared conditions; teacher feedback uses the four criteria. Not a Writing Screener.
blocks.prompt: The maps below show the village of Westhill in 1995 and today. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.

figure.title: Westhill village
figure.alt: Two maps of Westhill village. In 1995, farmland covered the north-west, a forest the north-east, a row of shops lay south of the main road in the west, a small school in the south-east, and a river ran along the southern edge. Today, the farmland has become a housing estate, part of the forest has been cleared for a sports centre, the shops have been replaced by a supermarket with a car park beside it, the school has been extended, and a new road crosses the river by a bridge.

blocks.conditions: 20 minutes, in one sitting, without a dictionary, translator, AI tool or model. Write the start and finish time. Advanced transfer: submit a second response to a genuinely unseen visual or prompt, with no model, scaffold or feedback before completion; log timing and support separately.
blocks.support: Plan: Introduction (paraphrase) / Overview (direction of change + what stayed the same) / Body 1 (north of the road) / Body 2 (south of the road and the river).
blocks.extension: Include one sentence about what has not changed.
blocks.high_band: Produce a new 150+-word comparative map report in 20 minutes without a model. Organise by meaningful spatial contrasts, distinguish preserved from replaced features, and avoid unsupported speculation or inaccurate directional language.
blocks.model_label: Illustrative model for teacher discussion after learners submit their own responses. Not a certified band answer.
blocks.model:
The maps compare the layout of the village of Westhill in 1995 with its appearance today.

Overall, Westhill has become considerably more developed, with much of its farmland and forest giving way to housing and leisure facilities, although the main road and the river remain unchanged.

The most striking changes have taken place to the north of the main road. The farmland that occupied the north-west of the village has been converted into a large housing estate. To the east of this, part of the forest has been cleared to make way for a new sports centre, so that only a smaller area of woodland remains in the north-east corner.

To the south of the road, the row of shops has been replaced by a supermarket, and a car park has been built next to it on its eastern side. The school in the south-east has been extended, roughly doubling in size. Finally, a new road now runs south from the main road and crosses the river by a bridge, giving the village a second route in and out.
checklist: Task Achievement: Is there an overview of the most important changes (and what stayed the same)? Are changes reported accurately?
Coherence and Cohesion: Are changes grouped logically, for example by area of the village, and linked clearly?
Lexical Resource: Is the vocabulary of change precise (was replaced by, was converted into, was cleared, was extended, was constructed)?
Grammatical Range and Accuracy: Are passive forms and the past simple / present perfect used accurately, with location phrases (to the north of, in the south-east)?
Independent-transfer check: verify task coverage, accuracy of evidence or visual comparisons, quality of development, and unsupported claims; note conditions rather than inferring an IELTS band.

stages.title: Opening challenge: which overview works?
stages.student: Rank the three overviews before the reveal.
stages.teacher: Reveal the comments. Write the map overview formula: general direction of change + what stayed the same.
stages.say: A map overview describes the big picture of change, not a list.
stages.check: Learners can name the two parts of a map overview.

stages.title: Accurate or inaccurate?
stages.student: Check each sentence against the maps.
stages.teacher: Learners work alone for 6 minutes. Foundation learners first label compass directions.
stages.say: Check every location word against the map.

stages.title: Check and correct
stages.student: Check answers and correct the inaccurate sentences.
stages.teacher: Reveal. Build a change-verb bank on the board from the answers.
stages.say: Precise verbs of change make a map description clear.

stages.title: Plan your paragraphs
stages.student: Plan two body paragraphs by area: north and south of the main road.
stages.teacher: Show that grouping by area is clearer than going building by building in random order.

stages.title: Write independently
stages.student: Write the overview and the north paragraph in 15 minutes.
stages.teacher: Time 15 minutes. Do not show the model. Record any support used.
stages.say: Use the present perfect passive for changes up to today.
stages.check: Every learner has written both paragraphs.

stages.title: Compare with the model and the criteria
stages.student: Compare your paragraphs with the model and tick the checklist.
stages.teacher: Show the model. Ask learners to find three different ways of describing change.
stages.say: The model is for discussion, not for memorising.
stages.check: Each learner has one specific improvement.

stages.title: Full Task 1 at home
stages.student: Note the homework conditions and the plan.
stages.say: Homework under real conditions shows what you can do alone.

stages.title: Exit ticket
stages.teacher: Collect exit tickets. Record the fresh-check date.
stages.say: Next time: charts that combine pies and tables.

blocks.title: Seaview Park then and now
blocks.prompt: Look at the two plans of Seaview Park, from 2000 and the present day. Summarise the key developments in an overview and one detailed paragraph.

figure.title: Seaview Park
figure.alt: Two maps of Seaview Park. In 2000, there was a tennis court in the north-west, a pond in the north-east, a large lawn in the south and a single entrance in the west. Today, the tennis court has become a children's playground, the pond remains with a new café beside it, part of the lawn has been made into a car park, and a second entrance has been added in the east.
